The source statement by itself therefore does not entail that stronger quantitative specialization.

findings.source_evidence: PDF page 19 says only that c(K)>0 may depend solely on K.
findings.translation_evidence: The blind translation fixes c(K)=(C(1+K))^(-3) with one universal C>=1 and separately proves its positivity.
findings.impact: The target is not logically equivalent to the literal source wording, but it entails the full source claim and preserves all of its objects, hypotheses, both inequalities, and uniformity requirements.

rationale: The blind translation accurately retains the inherited finite independent sub-gaussian, centered, unit-variance family; arbitrary real coefficients; K as the maximum psi-two gauge; the L1 norm of the weighted sum; the Euclidean coefficient norm; exact upper constant 1; the zero-coefficient case; and a strictly positive lower coefficient depending only on K. Its only material departure is beneficial and one-directional: it replaces the unspecified source quantity c(K) by the explicit universal inverse-cubic form (C(1+K))^(-3). Thus the translation clearly implies the source, whereas the source's qualitative existence statement does not imply this specific rate.
